eligibility: Must hold a valid Bond University Letter of Offer for a PhD or Professional Doctorate of Occupational Therapy before the scholarship application is considered
Must be studying the program full time
Open to Australian and international applicants
Cannot apply while receiving an equivalent Commonwealth award designed to offset higher degree research fees
existing.eligibility_summary: For domestic and overseas doctoral students who hold a valid Bond University Letter of Offer for a PhD or the Professional Doctorate of Occupational Therapy and will study full time. Applicants cannot apply if they already hold an equivalent Commonwealth award designed to offset higher degree research fees.
benefits: 100 per cent of program fees waived for four years
Living stipend of $34,315 per annum (2025 annual value, indexed annually) for three years
Single overseas health cover for international students, four years
coverage: 100 per cent fee waiver for up to four years
Living stipend of AUD 34,315 per annum, indexed annually, for three years
Single overseas health cover for international students for four years
requirements: Submit a Bond application for the program before applying for the scholarship
Use the Bond online scholarship application form
Applicants who have previously applied unsuccessfully may submit one additional application outlining changed circumstances; a second unsuccessful application ends eligibility
application_method: Submit a Bond application for an eligible doctoral program
Apply online using the Bond University Higher Degree Scholarship Application form
Submit before the round closure date, as late applications are not accepted
existing.selection_notes: The Bond University HDR Scholarships Committee meets biannually to award fee waivers and living stipends on a merit-based selection process. Applications are assessed by the Bond University Research Scholarship Panel against published selection criteria.
existing.best_fit: Doctoral candidates, including international students, who already have a Bond offer of place and need both full tuition and a living stipend to commit to a full-time PhD on the Gold Coast.
existing.notes:
Bond University allocates its own funds to support the financial costs of the fee offset and living stipends. The scholarship page notes that stipends are intended to support day-to-day expenses and do not include tuition fees. Research master's students are not eligible for any Bond higher degree research scholarship. No bond or service obligation is stated.
Funding period: per annum (2025 annual value on the scholarship page, indexed annually; Bond's fees and scholarships page gives the 2026 full-time rate as $34,315 AUD)
existing.duration: Living stipend for 3 years, which cannot be extended beyond that term; fee waiver for 4 years
existing.application_period: Higher degree research scholarship rounds are held twice per year, opening 1 February and closing 31 March, then opening 1 August and closing 30 September. The 2026 round closed on 30 September 2026; the next window opens 1 February 2027.
existing.deadline_display: 31 March 2027 (next round); rounds close 31 March and 30 September each year

eligibility: Must be a domestic student or an overseas student enrolled in an accredited research higher degree at ACU
Proposed research must align with any of ACU's broad areas of expertise
Undertaking a Research Doctorate or Research Masters degree
existing.eligibility_summary: Open to all applicants, domestic or overseas, who are enrolled in an accredited research higher degree at ACU and whose proposed research aligns with any of ACU's broad areas of expertise. Covers a Research Doctorate or Research Masters degree.
benefits: Stipend scholarship of AUD $34,315 per annum (full-time)
Full fee offset valued at approximately AUD $34,728 per annum
A single Overseas Student Health Care Policy
Relocation allowance of up to AUD $2,000 for international applicants
coverage: Stipend of AUD 34,315 per annum (full-time, 2026 value, indexed annually)
Full fee offset valued at approximately AUD 34,728 per annum
Single Overseas Student Health Care Policy
Relocation allowance of up to AUD 2,000 for international applicants
requirements: Be enrolled, or apply to enrol, in an accredited research higher degree at ACU
Complete the ACU Research Training Program Scholarship Policy requirements
Current students must submit the scholarship application form from the Student Portal with supporting documentation to the Graduate Research School
application_method: Prospective students apply as part of the application process for a research degree at ACU
Current students download the scholarship application form from the Student Portal and email it with supporting documentation to the Graduate Research School
existing.selection_notes: The scholarships are competitive and awarded following a merit-based selection process, with candidates judged on strong academic credentials and research potential. The award is funded by the Australian Catholic University and administered in accordance with the ACU Research Training Program Scholarship Policy.
existing.best_fit: Research doctorate or research master's candidates at ACU, domestic or international, whose project fits one of ACU's areas of expertise and who need tuition plus living costs, with international applicants also receiving a relocation allowance and overseas student health cover.
existing.notes: The stipend value is the 2026 figure and is indexed annually. No bond or service obligation is stated. Online study is not eligible for ACU's separate Vice-Chancellor's PhD Excellence Scholarship, which shares this funding base.
existing.duration: Stipend and full fee offset for the duration of the research degree, to a maximum of 3.5 years for a PhD
existing.application_period: Applications open twice per annum, in April and in October. Round 1 closed 1 April 2026 and Round 2 closed 1 October 2026, so the next window is the April 2027 round. Domestic commencements are the first workday of the following August, international commencements the first day of Research Term D in October for the April round and Research Term C in July for the October round.
existing.deadline_display: 1 April 2027 (next round); rounds close 1 April and 1 October each year
